title: Sponsor Oversight of CROs and Vendors: FDA BIMO and EMA GCP Inspection Findings
summary: FDA BIMO and EMA GCP inspection findings on sponsor oversight of CROs and vendors, with the recurring deficiencies set against ICH E6(R3) expectations.
body_markdown:
## Sponsor oversight of CROs and vendors: what FDA BIMO and EMA GCP inspections have cited


FDA Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO) inspections and EMA-requested GCP inspections apply the same accountability principle, with different regulatory consequences. A sponsor can outsource trial activities, but it cannot outsource accountability for them. Across FDA warning letters, Form FDA 483 observations in Drugs@FDA clinical inspection summaries, and GCP inspection outcomes reported in EPARs, the oversight findings fall into a small number of recurring patterns:


- Transfers of obligations that were missing, undocumented or unreported, or that the sponsor wrongly assumed had taken place.
- Monitoring delegated to a CRO without the sponsor checking that it actually happened, or that it worked.
- Sponsors that failed to act when CRO monitors reported investigator noncompliance.
- Weak oversight of data management, randomization and other system vendors, including subcontractors.
- Oversight failures serious enough that, in the EU, regulators treated pivotal data as unreliable, a heavier consequence than a citation.


### The regulatory baseline: delegation without abdication


ICH E6(R3) lets a sponsor transfer trial-related activities to a CRO or other service provider. The sponsor cannot transfer ultimate responsibility for participant protection or data reliability, and any activity not specifically transferred stays with the sponsor[50](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=50)[51](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=51) . The guideline expects the sponsor to:


- record transferred activities in an agreement and select capable providers[50](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=50)[52](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=52)
- have access to provider SOPs and performance metrics[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=53)
- oversee important transferred activities, including activities the provider subcontracts further[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=53)


Under US drug regulations, FDA has repeatedly said that monitoring may be transferred to a CRO only if the transfer is described in writing under 21 CFR 312.52[298](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060600/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm445817.htm)[20](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423061938/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2016/ucm497595.htm)[299](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060531/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm474234.htm) . A CRO that assumes sponsor obligations faces the same regulatory action as a sponsor if it fails to perform them[294](https://web.archive.org/web/20150921003920/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm193156.htm)[295](https://web.archive.org/web/20150921003920/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm193156.htm) . The device framework differs: FDA's BIMO compliance program notes that the device regulations do not provide for transfers of sponsor obligations to CROs[283](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=283) . In device warning letters FDA has stated that monitoring may be delegated, but the sponsor remains ultimately responsible for it[185](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048200.htm) .


### How inspectors evaluate oversight


**FDA.** Compliance Program 7348.810, *Sponsors, Contract Research Organizations and Monitors* , directs investigators to evaluate how the sponsor oversees outsourced services. The focus is on services that are critical to efficacy or safety data, or that are linked to significant regulatory deviations[280](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=280)[281](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=281) . Investigators check:


- whether the sponsor has criteria for selecting CROs and vendors, including an assessment of their ability to comply with FDA regulations and GCP[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=282)
- whether agreements define roles and regulatory responsibilities[282](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=282)
- the written transfer-of-obligations documents, and whether the required statement was submitted to FDA. Unreported transfers are documented[283](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=283) .


The program names site monitoring as a critical outsourced service[284](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=284) .


**EU.** EudraLex Volume 10 describes sponsor and CRO inspections as either system inspections or trial-specific inspections[212](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=212)[228](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=228) . Inspectors examine:


- procedures for selecting and continually assessing contractors and subcontractors[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=229)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=230)
- documentation of which duties were delegated, and when[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=229)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=230)
- how trial-related work done by contractors and subcontractors is overseen, and a sample of contracts[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=230)[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=231)
- the audit program for contractors, and the sponsor's or CRO's review of monitoring reports[232](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=232)[233](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=233)


Findings are graded critical, major or minor, and the inspection report gives an overall conclusion on GCP acceptability[234](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=234)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=223) .


### FDA BIMO findings


#### 1. Transfers of obligations that were missing, undocumented or unreported


- **Verdure Sciences (warning letter, November 10, 2025).** Verdure argued that its clinical study agreement had transferred sponsor obligations to a third-party vendor. FDA disagreed. The agreement named Verdure as "Sponsor" and the vendor as "Service Provider," and it did not specify any transferred obligations. A clause requiring the vendor to follow the protocol and applicable law was not enough to transfer them. Verdure therefore remained responsible for having an IND in effect, which it did not[296](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/verdure-sciences-inc-717259-11102025)[297](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/verdure-sciences-inc-717259-11102025) .
- **ICON Clinical Research (warning letter, November 27, 2009).** The contracts transferred site monitoring, protocol-violation tracking and source-document verification to the CRO. FDA cited the CRO directly under 21 CFR 312.50, 312.52 and 312.56(a)[294](https://web.archive.org/web/20150921003920/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm193156.htm)[295](https://web.archive.org/web/20150921003920/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm193156.htm) .
- **Angela D. Ritter, M.D. (warning letter, June 7, 2024).** In an expanded-access setting, the sponsor-investigator said she had relied on a CRO for IND maintenance, FDA correspondence, IRB submissions and annual reports. FDA held that she remained ultimately responsible for oversight and compliance[315](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/angela-d-ritter-md-681999-06072024)[316](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/angela-d-ritter-md-681999-06072024)[319](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/angela-d-ritter-md-681999-06072024)[320](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/angela-d-ritter-md-681999-06072024)[321](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/angela-d-ritter-md-681999-06072024) .
- **DOTAREM (clinical inspection summary).** A problem with the transfer-of-obligations notification was discussed verbally with the sponsor but was not cited on a Form FDA 483[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=369) . Transfer documentation is checked even when it does not produce a written observation.


#### 2. Monitoring delegated, but not overseen


- **Johnson & Johnson PRD (warning letter, August 10, 2009).** J&J contracted out monitoring visits, but FDA found the sites were not adequately monitored. Monitors missed drug-accountability and case-history deficiencies, including records showing study drug given to different subjects at exactly the same time[21](https://web.archive.org/web/20151006230625/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2009/ucm177398.htm) .
- **Pfizer (warning letter, April 9, 2010).** FDA cited a repeat failure to ensure proper monitoring. Widespread overdosing across sites went undetected and uncorrected[312](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604100228/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2010/ucm208976.htm) .
- **TCA Cellular Therapy (warning letter, August 15, 2011).** The contracted monitor stopped performing. The sponsor later found that the last monitoring visit had taken place in August 2008[313](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604132907/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm268796.htm)[314](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604132907/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm268796.htm) .
- **FIRDAPSE (NDA 208078).** After CRO monitoring responsibility changed hands, neither the sponsor nor the CRO made a monitoring visit for at least a year[360](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=360) .
- **SUBLOCADE (NDA 209819).** Most obligations had been transferred to a CRO. The sponsor still failed to perform the monitoring-oversight functions it had kept under its own plan, and inadequate drug accountability went undetected until after closeout[363](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=363) .
- **NUPLAZID (NDA 207318).** The sponsor gave its CRO a complete, final monitoring plan only after sites had been initiated and subjects enrolled[357](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=357) .
- **AMZEEQ (NDA 212379).** The sponsor relied on the CRO's SOPs for monitoring, and monitors missed significant site noncompliance[361](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=361)[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=362) .
- **Device sponsors.**


- Orthometrix: a contracted monitor overlooked eligibility miscalculations, and FDA asked for a corrective-action plan from the *sponsor*[187](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013121718/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075475.htm)[188](https://web.archive.org/web/20151013121718/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2005/ucm075475.htm) .
- Silimed: the plan named a central monitor who had made no on-site visit since 2003 and had delegated audits to regional CRAs without documentation[189](https://web.archive.org/web/20150603182642/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076372.htm) .
- Alan L. Schneider, M.D.: FDA rejected a proposal to use an outside monitoring group that came with no qualification procedure and no oversight plan[185](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630073833/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2008/ucm1048200.htm) .


#### 3. Not acting on what CRO monitors reported


FDA treats a sponsor's failure to act on CRO-identified problems as a failure to secure investigator compliance:


- **Rezurock (NDA 214783).** Kadmon received a Form 483 for not bringing a noncompliant site into compliance promptly. Twenty-one of 24 interim monitoring reports showed inadequate oversight, including missing source data, unassessed adverse events and unreported deviations[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=133) .
- **Poteligeo (BLA 761051).** The CRO monitor had flagged problems with investigator oversight, delegation logs and source-data verification. The sponsor received a 483 for not bringing the persistently noncompliant site into compliance or terminating it[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=135) .
- **Kyprolis (NDA 202714).** The sponsor's procedures for reviewing CRO-identified protocol deviations, and for handling repeated deviations reported by monitors, were inadequate[358](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=358) .
- **Duavee (NDA 022247).** Pfizer was classified VAI for delays in bringing investigators into compliance and in reviewing site monitoring reports. The CRO was classified NAI[139](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=139) .
- **Device sponsors.** Orthocon kept working with an investigator who had enrolled ineligible subjects after CRO visits documented the problem[186](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604135434/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm239310.htm) . BSD Medical brought in a CRO to supplement monitoring but still did not resolve a noncompliant investigator's deviations[190](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630013704/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076317.htm)[191](https://web.archive.org/web/20150630013704/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2007/ucm076317.htm) .


#### 4. Data, randomization and system vendors


Several clinical inspection summaries trace data problems to vendors:


- **Rezurock.** A data-management CRO made dataset-export errors[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=134) .
- **Goprelto (NDA 209963).** A CRO transposed the 4% and 8% dose groups in the NDA data. The sponsor found and corrected the error[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=137) .
- **Trulance (NDA 208745).** A CRO's eligibility portal miscalculated around daylight-saving time, and data-system problems led the sponsor to migrate to another CRO's system[138](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=138) .
- **Praluent (BLA 125559).** Randomization and titration errors required corrective and preventive action by the sponsor and its vendors[130](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=130) .


In these cases the sponsor's detection and correction appear to have supported data acceptability. That outcome depends on oversight being able to catch the error.


#### 5. Substituting other bodies for sponsor monitoring


FDA has rejected reliance on bodies that cannot take over the sponsor's monitoring duties:


- **Oeyama-Moto (2016).** The sponsor pointed to IRB minutes; FDA said an IRB cannot assume the monitoring responsibility[20](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423061938/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2016/ucm497595.htm) .
- **Henry Lin, M.D. (2010).** FDA found that the DSMB documents addressed adverse events, not protocol compliance[19](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604101856/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2010/ucm204453.htm) .
- **CXL-USA (2015) and Thomas Tooma, M.D. (2015).** Site "self-monitoring" and reliance on surgeons were not accepted as monitoring[298](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060600/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm445817.htm)[299](https://web.archive.org/web/20190423060531/https://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2015/ucm474234.htm) .


#### What adequate oversight looked like


Clinical inspection summaries also record positive outcomes:


- **Besremi (BLA 761166).** The sponsor's monitoring plan and trial oversight were adequate[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=128) .
- **Triferic (NDA 206317).** The CRO's oversight was found generally adequate after its audits led to two noncompliant sites being discontinued[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=129) .
- **Signifor LAR (NDA 203255).** The CRO was classified NAI[127](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=127) .


### EMA GCP inspection findings reported in EPARs


The EU findings show the same failure modes. The EPARs often report the consequence for the assessment directly.


Product Oversight-related finding Effect on the assessment


Ranluspec / Vislyfa Major finding: inadequate vendor management. Neither the global CRO nor its subcontracted vendors had been considered for risk-based auditing[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=255)[325](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=325)[326](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=326) Reported alongside a separate critical site finding on manipulated IOP metadata[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=255)


Alsitek / Masitinib AB Science Critical findings on sponsor/CRO trial management and clinical monitoring[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=156)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=157) Data from the inspected sites judged not reliable enough to support authorisation[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=156)[157](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=157)


VeraSeal Critical CRO performance; limited sponsor/affiliate review of safety information that was the monitoring CRO's responsibility, and ultimately the sponsor's[260](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=260)[261](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=261) Efficacy and safety data deemed unacceptable[260](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=260)[261](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=261)


Vimpat Sponsor and CRO performance not GCP-compliant[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=262)[263](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=263) Data from the Croatian site unreliable[262](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=262)[263](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=263)


Gamifant Data collection, management and analysis findings attributed mainly to inadequate sponsor oversight[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=163) Study NI-0501-04 considered non-GCP-compliant and unsuitable for evaluation[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=163)


Scenesse Problems with sponsor and sponsor/CRO data handling and statistical planning[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=151) Main efficacy data from CUV029/CUV030 judged unreliable; applicant submitted another trial[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=151)


Omontys Insufficient oversight and monitoring[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=264) Reported with data-handling irregularities and concerns about the per-protocol population[264](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=264)


Pradaxa Inadequate oversight and documentation of database edit checks at the CRO; poor oversight of delegated tasks[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=164) Findings not expected to affect overall results[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=164)


Yervoy / Opdivo (CA209227) Deficiencies at the sponsor and CRO in controlling information access within an immature risk-management system[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=159)[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=160) Trial integrity of CA209227 could not be ascertained for one target population[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=159)[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=161)


Onpattro Concerns about trial management, monitoring, data management and audit trails led to inspection of the CRO[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=158)[266](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=266) Efficacy assessments for 12 patients excluded; results remained consistent[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=158)


Imfinzi / Imjudo (POSEIDON) One critical finding at the main CRO (not specified in the EPAR)[257](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=257)[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=258)[259](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=259) Considered unlikely to affect overall data quality[257](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=257)


Reasanz Eight major findings, but trial oversight across multiple monitoring CROs judged adequate, including through a change of sponsor[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=265) Oversight not a basis for concern[265](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=265)


### Cross-cutting lessons for sponsors


- **Write down the transfer, and report it where required.** Inspectors read the agreements. A "service provider" clause did not transfer sponsor obligations in the Verdure letter[296](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/verdure-sciences-inc-717259-11102025)[297](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/verdure-sciences-inc-717259-11102025) , and FDA investigators document unreported transfers[283](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=283) .
- **Keep retained functions visible.** SUBLOCADE and Ritter show that when most obligations go to a CRO, the obligations the sponsor keeps are the ones most likely to lapse[363](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=363)[319](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/angela-d-ritter-md-681999-06072024) .
- **Treat changes of CRO or monitor as high-risk events.** The FIRDAPSE and TCA findings both followed a change or loss of the monitoring provider[360](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=360)[314](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604132907/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm268796.htm) .
- **Act on monitoring reports.** Several 483s were issued even though the CRO had correctly identified the problem; the sponsor simply did not escalate or close the site[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=133)[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=135)[186](https://web.archive.org/web/20150604135434/http://www.fda.gov/ICECI/EnforcementActions/WarningLetters/2011/ucm239310.htm) .
- **Extend oversight to subcontractors and system vendors.** ICH E6(R3) expects this[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=53) . EU inspectors graded its absence as a major finding in Ranluspec[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=255) , and EudraLex Volume 10 makes subcontractor assessment an explicit inspection subject[229](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=229)[230](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=230) .
- **Expect different consequences in each jurisdiction.** In the FDA material reviewed here, oversight failures often led to warning letters or 483s while the data were still accepted[132](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=132)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=133) . In several EPARs, though not all, the same kind of failure led CHMP to treat pivotal data as unreliable[156](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=156)[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=163)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=151)[260](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsor-oversight-of-cros-and-vendors-what-fda?showSourceNumber=260) .


Many of the FDA warning letters that directly address CRO monitoring date from 2005 to 2016 and were issued under 21 CFR Part 312 and earlier versions of ICH E6, not E6(R3). More recent sponsor-oversight findings appear mainly as 483 observations in clinical inspection summaries. Useful follow-up questions for Rhizome include how often these findings cluster by therapeutic area or application type, how inspectors handled transfer-of-obligations statements for specific products, and how sponsor responses were evaluated in particular closeout letters.
